headline: Nvidia releases open Cosmos 3 models to simulate worlds
dek: The models simulate robotics and driving, per Nvidia.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: Cosmos 3
body: Nvidia released new open-weight models in its Cosmos 3 family to simulate robotics and driving scenes, per Hugging Face.
They are versions of Cosmos 3 Nano, with 16 billion parameters each (Hugging Face).

points.t: Video across up to 11 cameras (Hugging Face).
Creates point clouds aligned to the images.
One variant generates chunks in sequence.

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: What they are for
body: In robotics, one variant predicts the visual result of an action, per Nvidia (Hugging Face).
In driving, it varies roads and signals to test policies.

items.t: Teams can train on their own sensor setups (Hugging Face).
Where the models fall short is still unmeasured (Hugging Face).

caption.hook: Nvidia released open Cosmos 3 models to simulate robotics and driving scenes.
body: Per Nvidia on Hugging Face, the models are versions of Cosmos 3 Nano, with 16 billion parameters each, and can be used in commercial or non-commercial projects. Transfer-Auto makes synchronized video across up to 11 cameras, plus LiDAR point clouds, the laser sensor data that maps distance and shape.

Sim-Auto is a real-time variant that generates video chunks in sequence for interactive simulations. In robotics, another variant predicts the visual result of an action. The company admits it still needs to measure how far the models can support training for robots and self-driving vehicles.
caption.cta: Would you train a robot on AI-generated data?
